title: Live routing fallback controller for private data-plane upgrades
creator: Ava Patel
description: Objective: implement a controller for Private (VPC) data-plane upgrades that performs live routing with an intelligent fallback path to guarantee zero-downtime for tenant traffic while enabling deterministic, auditable rollback. The controller is implemented as a Terraform-hooked operator plus a runtime sidecar that manages per-tenant routing rules, lightweight hedged requests, and health-quorum assertions. This ticket covers design, Terraform module changes, operator implementation, telemetry, and runbook/QA for the first supported upgrade surface (runtime binary + kernel-change release).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can perform a staged traffic shift per-tenant with 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% progression driven by synthetic probe success
If health quorum dips below threshold or latency spikes > 2x baseline for 3m, traffic is automatically routed to fallback variant within 30s

Rollback action (automated or manual) restores previous routing rules and KV cache reconciliation is initiated, with no more than 1% request error increase observed across tenants during rollbacks in test clusters
Terraform modules expose declarative inputs: rollout_policy, health_quorum, probe_profiles, and fallback_model_map; documentation and examples added
Telemetry dashboards show per-route RTT, error%, probe success rate, traffic fraction, and rollback events; alerts created for SLO violations
Security review completed and operator has least-privilege IAM/Terraform plan with audit logging enabled
implementation_notes: Architecture: split into (1) terraform-managed operator deployment + RBAC/KMS bindings, (2) in-cluster controller that updates Envoy/sidecar routing rules, (3) lightweight runtime sidecar that can return fast failover responses and trigger KV rewarm hooks
Routing model: per-tenant virtual host with weighted clusters; use hedging window to probe new cluster while maintaining baseline traffic to old cluster
Health quorum: combine active synthetic probes, passive latency/error sampling, and KV priming completion state. Default quorum = 0.95 across these signals
Fallback selection: map of compatible model variants maintained in CRD and referenced by terraform; allow fallbacks to lower-capacity but high-availability variants
Terraform: add module 'private/upgrade-controller' exposing lifecycle hooks (preflight, post-deploy-probe, rollback-hook) and remote-state outputs for controller to consume
Safety: controller must support manual pause, forced rollback, and staged resume. All state transitions are persisted in CRD with timestamps for audit
KV cache: on successful migration, trigger parallel KV snapshot/restore jobs for warmed prefixes. Provide fast-path request header to bypass cold-start penalties during transition
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dry-run in staging cluster. Deploy operator via terraform module with rollout_policy disabled. Validate CRD lifecycle and probe profiles.

Stage 1: Canary tenants (internal customers): enable 1% of traffic to new runtime variant for 1h. Run synthetic probe suite (1000 qps synthetic) and real traffic shadowing. Verify KV priming completes for top 10 prefixes.
Stage 2: Incremental ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Advance only if probe success and latency within thresholds.
Stage 3: Full cutover and post-cutover monitor for 6h. If any rollback condition fires, controller routes full traffic back to fallback and triggers reconcile jobs.
Controls: terraform can set max_traffic_step, min_observation_window, and cooldown timers. Enable automatic panic mode that sets traffic_fraction=0 for failing cluster and notifies on-call.
Coordination: schedule with platform on-call and notify affected customers via pager-duty channel and status page. Share PRD and runbook link before each major stage.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback: triggered when health_quorum < 0.9 OR 99th-percentile latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive observation windows. Controller flips routing weights back within 30s and marks CRD state as 'rolled_back'.
Manual rollback: on-call can run terraform apply with module variable 'force_rollback=true' which calls operator rollback-hook to rebind previous clusters and initiate KV reconciliation

KV reconciliation: start parallel warmup jobs using latest snapshot; if warmup fails for critical prefixes after 15m, controller will divert traffic to the previous variant's cold path with throttling to avoid cascading failures
Post-rollback verification: run 30m smoke tests and a targeted regression eval suite against affected tenants. Capture traces for failure analysis and attach to incident ticket
Audit: all rollback events must include rationale, triggering metrics, and linked terraform plan IDs for traceability
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller state machine and Terraform hooks
Integration tests in staging that simulate: probe failures, slow KV rewarm, increased error rates, and API-level golden-path traffic
Chaos tests: random node reboots, network partitions, and GC spikes during a live rollout to validate controller stabilization logic
Performance tests: measure additional P50/P95 latency introduced by hedging and sidecar routing under realistic token lengths
End-to-end dry-run: run through full rollout/rollback in an isolated environment and validate metrics and alerts fire as expected
Customer canary: coordinate with one low-risk customer to run a trial upgrade with detailed telemetry access
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tenant traffic fraction, probe success rate, kv_warm_prefix_count, p50/p95 latency, error rate, rollout_state timeline
SLOs: maintain request success rate >= 99.9% during rollouts; alert on 5m breach
Logs: structured operator events written to audit-log with rollout_id, step, and tenant_set
Tracing: propagate rollout_id in traces for request correlation across clusters
risks_mitigation: Risk: KV cold starts causing client timeouts — Mitigation: conservative traffic ramp and background warmup jobs with priority scheduling
Risk: operator misconfiguration via Terraform — Mitigation: strict schema validation, plan output checks, and gate applying terraform with CI policy
Risk: cascading failure during rollback — Mitigation: introduce throttled rollback path with token-bucket limiter and incremental revert windows
Risk: unauthorized operator action — Mitigation: least-privilege IAM, signed terraform plans, and audit log retention
Risk: probe false-positives — Mitigation: composite quorum using multiple signals and an adaptive debounce window
